name_note: GTDB uses Mediterraneibacter lactaris, the name proposed when Ruminococcus lactaris was reclassified; most literature still calls it Ruminococcus lactaris.

sentences.text: It is a bacterium found in the human gut, detected in faecal samples and in metagenomic data on faecal specimens.
In an in vitro study using faecal samples as inocula, sequences related to Ruminococcus lactaris were among those most commonly recovered from porcine gastric mucin, an insoluble substrate.
A study reported that, in nine healthy male adults ingesting flaxseeds for one week, enterolactone production was linked to the abundance of Ruminococcus bromii and Ruminococcus lactaris.

Reported health links include enrichment of Ruminococcus lactaris in controls among Nigerians, and decreased average abundance has been reported in the microbiota of children with autism spectrum disorder.
